openDecisions.question: Shape of the notesCount contract
options: A1: detail-only BookDetailsViewSchema = BookViewSchema.extend({ notesCount }) on GET /api/books/:id; FE detail-cache writers merge the previous notesCount
A2: optional notesCount on BookViewSchema, filled for single-book responses (getById and the loadView paths)
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: A1: one count call in getById, and two FE writers need a merge (use-book-mutation-sync.ts:17, use-toggle-favorite-dedication.ts:27). A2 needs a count on about 20 single-book response paths (17 loadView calls, getById, update at books.service.ts:359); one missed path drops the badge
openDecisions.recommendation: A1: the field is required where it is guaranteed, BookView stays untouched, and mutations pay no extra COUNT
openDecisions.answeredBy: assumption: recommendation adopted per package rule (stop only on fundamental conflict), 2026-10-17

openDecisions.question: How to get page ASC NULLS LAST, createdAt DESC, id ASC for the tab
options: Global tie-break: BOOK_NOTE_SORT_ORDER_BY.page = [bookTitle, page, newest, id]
New sort value (e.g. page_in_book) in BookNoteSortSchema
Implicit order switch when exactly one book is in scope
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: Option 1 is one line plus note-sort.test.ts:48; the old id tie-break was arbitrary because Note.id is a random uuid(). Option 2 leaks into the global archive sort menu (sortOptions = BookNoteSortSchema.options, notes-archive-config.ts:42) and needs gen:api. Option 3 is hidden behavior
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1, documented as an intentional global tie-break change
openDecisions.answer: Option 1 (global page tie-break newest before id, documented)
openDecisions.answeredBy: assumption: recommendation adopted per package rule (stop only on fundamental conflict), 2026-10-17

openDecisions.question: How to stop a query for the book's own title from matching every note in the tab
options: Explicit opt-in query param on list and facets (the default keeps archive semantics)
Implicit: skip book-metadata conditions when book has exactly one id
Leave as is and accept FIND-02 failing
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: The explicit param is one enum in bookNotesDatasetQueryFields (notes.ts:130), shared by both schemas, plus one branch at book-notes-where.ts:84. The implicit option changes the global archive's 'show book notes' flow (use-notes-archive-query.ts:107-108 sets book=[id]), which E.1 forbids
openDecisions.recommendation: Explicit param; confirm the name (proposal: searchIn = notes_and_book | notes)
openDecisions.answer: Explicit param searchIn = notes_and_book | notes, default notes_and_book
openDecisions.answeredBy: assumption: recommendation adopted per package rule (stop only on fundamental conflict), 2026-10-17

options: No backend change; the tab ignores the book/author dimensions
Add a flag that skips the two extra aggregations
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: No change: notes-facets.service.ts:29-38 already runs the four queries in parallel, and the spec forbids optimising an unmeasured cost
openDecisions.recommendation: No change now; revisit only if a facets call is measured as slow
openDecisions.answeredBy: assumption: recommendation adopted per package rule (stop only on fundamental conflict), 2026-10-17

openDecisions.question: How to namespace the tab's URL keys

Reuse NOTES_ARCHIVE_PARSERS.books through a nuqs urlKeys mapping

assumptions: Quick-filter label stays the existing archive label (Улюблені) per contract C "existing labels"; decision #04 lists it as Обрані.
NotesArchiveContent prop keeps its name view (not layout) so archive call sites compile unchanged; embedded added as a third value.
S1 review Low 4 (shared writeBookDetail helper) not applied: two uses, project extracts on the third.

Scroll anchor (#08) is captured synchronously in BookDetailsView.changeTab when leaving notes, not from scroll events: a real Chromium run showed the per-scroll capture being overwritten by the scroll clamp of the shorter tab. Leaving via browser back/forward does not restore (the anchor is only captured on a tab click).

Because Book Details tabs are not sticky, a user always scrolls up to the tablist before switching; in real runs the restore keeps the same top card at the same offset (desktop and 390px), and the neighbour/scrollY fallbacks are unit-tested only.

A11y pre-existing, out of scope (shared components): mobile-sort-sheet focus return and label-in-name, facet-multiselect aria-checked, PageTabs tablist name, restore scroll on arrow-key tab activation.
